ask: TypeScript, React 18 types available. useDebouncedQuery.ts: hook that debounces a query string, cancels in-flight requests with AbortController, exposes {data, loading, error, refetch}, handles race conditions with a request id, and cleans up on unmount. include a usage comment block. write the file.
prose:
The file wrote successfully. `useDebouncedQuery.ts` is ready to use.

A few things worth noting about the implementation:

The request id counter (`requestIdRef`) is the core race-condition guard. Each call to `execute` increments it and captures the value before going async — any response that arrives after a newer request was fired will see a mismatch and bail out silently, so you'll never see a stale result land after a faster one.

The `AbortController` on top of that handles cleanup at the network layer. When a new query fires mid-flight, the old request gets aborted before the new one is created, so you're not just ignoring stale results — you're actively cancelling the work.

`refetch` skips the debounce timer and calls `execute` directly with the current query, which is the right behavior for a manual refresh action.

One thing to watch: `queryFn` is in the `useCallback` deps of `execute`. If you define the fetch function inline in the component without `useCallback`, it'll be a new reference every render and trigger more requests than intended. The usage comment shows the pattern to follow — define it outside the component or memoize it.
